# sugar

> Syntactic sugar: compound assignment, for-in loops and assertions.

[source](../../registry/sugar.pkg) · truck

Shorthands that `std` doesn't have. Every package here `expand`s into
`std` constructs, so they work with every backend and have no backend
packages of their own.

```
use std
use sugar

let total = 0
for n in make([int], 3)
  total += n + 1
end
assert total == 3
```

| package | syntax | becomes |
|---|---|---|
| `sugar/add_assign` | `x += y` | `x = x + y` |
| `sugar/sub_assign` | `x -= y` | `x = x - y` |
| `sugar/mul_assign` | `x *= y` | `x = x * y` |
| `sugar/div_assign` | `x /= y` | `x = x / y` |
| `sugar/mod_assign` | `x %= y` | `x = x % y` |
| `sugar/forin` | `for x in xs ... end` | a loop over a slice's elements or a string's bytes |
| `sugar/assert` | `assert cond` | stop with status 2 and the position if `cond` is false |

`sugar` is a separate truck, not part of `std`, so its words (`in`,
`assert`) are only reserved in programs that use it, and programs and
lock files that only use `std` are unaffected. Use single packages
(`use sugar/forin`) to take just one.
